title: Primary clarifier sludge withdrawal worked calculation (10 MLD, 400 mg/l SS, 60 % removal)
readable: SS removed per day = 10×400×0.6 = 2400 kg/day; solids concentration 2 %; volume to be drawn = 2400×(100/2)/1000 = 120 m3/day; continuous withdrawal = 120/24 = 5 m3/hr; pipe area for 200 mm dia = (0.2)×(0.2)×0.785 = 0.03 m2; velocity = 5 / 3600 / 0.03 = 0.04 m/s; withdrawal for 5 minutes every hour = 120 / (24×5/60) = 60 m3/hr; velocity = 60 / 3600 / 0.03 = 0.55 m/s

symbols.definition: inverse of the printed 2 % solids concentration
pipe diameter, m, for the printed 200 mm dia

applicability: Worked example of sludge withdrawal from a primary clarifier for a 10 MLD plant with 400 mg/l of SS and 60 % removal.
notes: Printed inline as a sequence of prose calculations, not as displayed or numbered equations; p359-1 is a service locator.
Two printed prose sentences interrupt the calculation: Clearly this cannot be permitted. and Obviously this is much better than withdrawal through a sludge sump.
The pipe area is printed as (0.2)×(0.2)×0.785 = 0.03 m2 twice, once for each withdrawal case.

transcription.method: Direct visual reading of full annotation-cleaned 144 dpi page PNGs, plus enlarged crops at 288-720 dpi and a contact sheet of every hashed source region; no OCR, no paid service, no delegation
transcription.observations: First visual transcription only. Every printed glyph, power, subscript, inequality, unit, hyphen spacing, footnote and printed error was read from the rendered source and retained or flagged; no value inferred.
